analysis:
Reviewed both primary analyses against the replayed patches and metadata. changelog.d/glm-variable-frame-rate-video.md:3 and docs/architecture/inference.md:810–813 (head) describe accepting variable-frame-rate media using presentation-order indices and nominalFrameRate-derived timestamps; head:829 removes the previous refusal. The documentation retains 2 FPS sampling, a 512 MiB retained decoded-frame cap, shared visual-token budgeting, media reservations and exclusion from prefix-cache reuse. No supported change to authorization, attestation, hop encryption, credentials, billing or privileged-helper controls is visible.
The added GLM5NextMediaRoutingTests.swift:256–309 test loads hash-checked local fixtures, normalizes inline media, runs GLM5NextProcessor, checks prepared grids/spans and reaches a scripted engine. Its preparation closure returns synthetic preparedSubmission(), so this verifies acceptance/routing rather than production embedding submission or resource safety. No concrete security regression is established by these documentation/test changes.
Material uncertainty remains: libs/mlx-swift-lm:1 advances the runtime dependency without supplying its implementation diff. Review the changed GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset path and MediaIngest interaction for finite positive frame-rate validation, malformed timestamps, bounded total decoding work/allocation, cancellation (T-010), token/reservation accounting (TB-007), and avoidance of plaintext temporary files (A-001, T-050). Confirm media prefix-cache exclusion remains effective (T-041). Accepting additional consumer-controlled decoder inputs makes these contracts material; positive fixtures cannot establish them. Replay also explicitly omits five previously reviewed source units, limiting independent verification. Deeper runtime review is required, not a finding inferred from missing source.
